summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic musculoskeletal chest pain, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, and inconsistent medication adherence was admitted for chest pain radiating to the back, abdominal pain, and worsening lower extremity edema. She had stopped her furosemide due to polyuria, leading to fluid retention. Initial evaluation showed no evidence of acute coronary syndrome, pulmonary embolism, or aortic dissection. Her hemoglobin was 6.8 g/dL, and she received two units of packed red blood cells due to acute on chronic anemia, though no active bleeding was found. Leukopenia and macrocytic anemia raised concern for myelodysplastic syndrome. Chronic interstitial lung disease was noted on imaging, but dyspnea improved with diuresis and supplemental oxygen. Pain management was optimized with scheduled acetaminophen. She was discharged home on her prior medications, including warfarin and furosemide, with plans for hematology follow-up and continued primary care management of her chronic pain and anemia.
problems: Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
